text: More than 2,500 years ago, the Sogdians farmed river valleys in today’s Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.
The kings of Persia ruled them, and they paid tribute, a kind of tax.
src: c. 6th century BCE, when Sogdiana appears in Persian inscriptions / the fertile valley of the Zeravshan / in present-day Uzbekistan and Tajikistan
Sogdiana enters recorded history as a province of the Achaemenid Empire / Herodotus lists the Sogdians among the peoples who paid tribute to the Persian king

text: Later, Sogdian merchants carried silk, silver, horses and enslaved people between Central Asia and China.
One of them, Maniakh, even led a journey to Justin II, the emperor in Constantinople.
src: From the 4th century CE at the latest, Sogdian merchants were the chief carriers of trade between Central Asia and China / They traded in silk, silver, musk, horses, slaves and much else
568: The Sogdian Maniakh leads a Turkic embassy to the emperor Justin II in Constantinople

text: Most Sogdians kept fire temples, but merchants also carried Buddhism and Manichaeism across Asia.
They won a Uyghur ruler to Manichaeism, which became his state’s religion.
src: They kept temples of fire / Sogdian merchants carried other faiths across Asia. Some were Buddhists / Others followed Manichaeism
Sogdian Manichaeans converted the Uyghur ruler Bögü Khagan in 762 or 763, making theirs the state religion of the Uyghur Khaganate

text: Painters covered the walls of halls with gods, feasts, hunts and heroes from old stories.
At Afrasiab, old Samarkand, one painted hall shows visitors from China and Korea.
src: the halls of houses were covered with scenes of gods, banquets, hunts and mourning, with episodes from epics

At Afrasiab, the old site of Samarkand / envoys from Chaghaniyan, Chach, China and the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo come to the court / a hall painted in the mid-7th century for Varkhuman, king of Samarkand

text: More than 1,300 years ago, Arab armies conquered Sogdiana.
One ruler fled to a fort on Mount Mugh, where his letters were found centuries later.
src: 712: The Arabs under Qutayba ibn Muslim take Samarkand / Conquered by the Arabs in the early 8th century
fled to a fortress on Mount Mugh in 722 / his archive, found in the ruins of the fortress in 1933, preserves letters and contracts in Sogdian, Arabic and Chinese

text: In time the Sogdians became Muslim and spoke Persian or Turkic.
Their alphabet lives on in the Mongolian script, which is still written today.
src: they became Muslim and Persian- or Turkic-speaking
their alphabet lives on, through the Uyghurs, in the Mongolian script / is thus still written in Inner Mongolia today
